Subject: Locality assurances and erasure expectations for Dedicated deployment

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Acme is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production slate of regulated workloads and legal asked me to confirm a couple of specifics before we move forward:

- Can you confirm that a Dedicated deployment can be hard-pinned to a single AWS region (we are looking at us-west-2) and that no customer content, snapshots, backups, or KV cache copies will be replicated outside that region?
- Does Redwood’s control plane ever store or traverse plaintext customer payloads? If so, what residency controls apply to control-plane metadata?
- What is your deletion/erasure process when we ask for full data deletion (including backups)? What are the expected timelines for primary storage, snapshots, and any cold/backups?
- For compliance we will need an evidence package (audit excerpt, deletion playbook, and a signed attestation). Can you provide those or point us to where they live?

Also, a quick question on billing metadata — do you retain invoice/billing metadata outside the pinned region? If yes, for how long?

Appreciate a concise set of commitments we can present to Legal.

Thanks,
Sara Lam
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme FinTech

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Locality assurances and erasure expectations for Dedicated deployment

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (Security) and Marissa (Solutions) to provide the formal artifacts. Below is a summary of our standard Dedicated commitments and how they map to your asks; we'll follow up with attachments and a short call if you want to walk through details.

Quick answers (summary):
- Region pinning: Yes. Dedicated instances can be hard-pinned to a single cloud region (e.g., AWS us-west-2). We do not replicate customer content, KV caches, or snapshots to other regions unless explicitly configured for DR by the customer.
- Control plane: The control plane stores routing/operational metadata only (instance IDs, model versions, routing policies). It never stores customer plaintext request payloads; all sensitive payloads transit encrypted-over-TLS and are stored encrypted-at-rest in the pinned region.
- Deletion/erasure timelines: On a verified deletion request we run a three-stage pipeline: 1) Evict in-memory KV/prefix caches immediately (within minutes); 2) Delete primary object storage and indices within 48 hours (subject to job queue/throughput); 3) Expire and delete encrypted backups/snapshots on the normal retention horizon but accelerate destruction: snapshots flagged for immediate destruction are removed from active storage within 30 days and any remaining snapshot keys are cryptographically shredded; we can provide a written attestation after completion.
- Billing/metadata: Billing invoices and billing metadata are stored for accounting and audit. Billing records are kept for 13 months by default and may be stored in a regional metadata store that is not part of the customer’s pinned data plane. If regional separation of billing metadata is required, we can discuss options (enterprise contracts).

Attachments we will share: dedicated-deletion-playbook.pdf (playbook + timelines), socs2-section-6.3.pdf (SOC 2 excerpt on data handling), and a geo-pin-checklist.xlsx (operational checklist to confirm the region pin).

Next steps:
1) Neha / Marissa to share the formal artifacts and a short attestation template by EOD.
2) If helpful, schedule a 30-minute technical call to walk the legal and infra teams through the deletion flow and provide a sample export package.

If you want anything more prescriptive (e.g., shorter backup destruction windows) we can discuss contract language and operational cost impacts.

— Jonas

Hi Sara — attaching the artifacts and answering your two bullets below. Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/acme/dedicated-data-flow (also in metadata).

Responses:
- Metadata telemetry: By default, request-level telemetry that is used for platform health is pseudonymized at ingestion (request IDs are hashed) and stored in our telemetry cluster; for Dedicated customers we offer a configuration to pin telemetry to the private control plane within the pinned region. If you require strict regional isolation of telemetry, we will enable region-local telemetry for Acme as part of the Dedicated onboarding (no additional charge for standard telemetry pinning).
- Snapshot attestation: Yes — once snapshots flagged for accelerated destruction complete their deletion workflow we will produce a signed attestation detailing deletion timestamps, the snapshot identifiers, and the cryptographic key destruction steps (key shredding / KMS rekey notation). That attestation will be included in the evidence package.

Attachments included: dedicated-deletion-playbook.pdf, socs2-section-6.3.pdf, geo-pin-checklist.xlsx

Proposed next step: 30-minute call next week with Acme infra and legal to walk the playbook and sign the deletion request. Jonas — can you propose 3 time slots?
